question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: one keyless tools/call of microsoft_docs_search, query "Azure Functions durable orchestration", to the endpoint with maxTokenBudget=notanumber, jsonrpc 2.0, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.what-it-answered: HTTP 200, 59003 raw bytes, 28958 content bytes (28958 characters, equal here because this content is pure ASCII), 10 results, content sha256 prefix 2db1a1ad986b7a2f.
decoded.the-vendor-claim-under-test: the vendor README, under Token Budget Control: "To manage token usage and control costs, you can append the maxTokenBudget query parameter to the MCP endpoint URL. This parameter limits the token count in search tool responses by truncating the content to meet your specified budget", marked experimental and "subject to change".
decoded.what-the-two-byte-counts-mean: two byte counts are reported because they measure different things: CONTENT bytes is the UTF-8 length of result.content[0].text, the documentation actually delivered, and RAW is the whole event-stream response. The content sha256 prefix is published so a reader can compare responses across these records without trusting a length. Only bytes were measured; the vendor's claim is about TOKENS and this record does not convert between them.
decoded.the-value-is-ignored-in-silence: 28,958 content bytes and 59,003 raw, content sha256 prefix 2db1a1ad986b7a2f, byte-identical to the unbudgeted response in the same pass (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-search-unbudgeted). A typo in the value of a documented cost-control parameter does not fail; it uncaps the response for a caller who believes it is capped.
decoded.why-this-is-the-more-interesting-of-the-: maxTokenBudget=0 is at least a number out of range (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-max-token-budget-zero). This value cannot be parsed at all, which is the case a server most easily rejects, and it is still accepted in silence.
decoded.the-control-is-its-own-record: an unknown TOOL name on this endpoint answers a proper JSON-RPC -32602 (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-unknown-tool-control).
decoded.third-instance-of-one-class-on-one-serve: the other two are an empty-argument search answered as an empty result set (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-refusals-as-success) and an out-of-scope fetch refusal delivered as content (p-20260930-microsoft-learn-mcp-fetch-out-of-scope).
decoded.not-measured: whether a misspelled parameter name behaves the same way; not tried, not claimed.
decoded.why-this-record-is-one-request: this pull request's records were split so that each is ONE request with one status and one surface, which is what the probe schema's own title says a probe is, after the registry's reviewer held the first head for bundling five different endpoint URLs under one observed.status and one surface. The comparison across budgets lives in the entry's profile and in the decoded fields here, each naming the sibling record it compares with.
decoded.which-reading-this-is: third reading. The five budget requests were sent once at about 12:15Z, again at 12:22:33Z when the raw byte counts were added, and again at 18:06Z as five separately captured requests. Every content and raw figure is identical across all three readings, six hours apart, so the search index behind this query did not move today.

finding: maxTokenBudget=notanumber, an unparseable value for a documented cost-control parameter, is accepted in silence: the keyless query returned 28,958 content bytes and 59,003 raw with content sha256 prefix 2db1a1ad986b7a2f, byte-identical to the unbudgeted response in the same pass, with no error, no isError and no warning. This is the more telling of the two invalid values, because an unparseable value is the case a server rejects most easily, and 0 at least is a number out of range. A typo in the value does not fail the call; it uncaps the response for a caller who believes it is capped. The control is a separate record: an unknown tool name here draws a proper -32602.

reproducibility.command: curl -s -X POST 'https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp?maxTokenBudget=notanumber' -H 'content-type: application/json' -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"microsoft_docs_search","arguments":{"query":"Azure Functions durable orchestration"}}}' | sed -n 's/^data: //p' | python3 -c 'import json,sys,hashlib;t=json.load(sys.stdin)["result"]["content"][0]["text"];print(len(t.encode()),len(json.loads(t)["results"]),hashlib.sha256(t.encode()).hexdigest()[:16])'
